findings.title: `import()` runs as soon as this module loads, so no app loading is deferred.
findings.body: Each property calls `import("./x")` when the object literal is built. Importing `@calcom/app-store` therefore starts loading all 28 app packages at once, which is what the old static imports did. The PR says it defers module loading, but it doesn't: no cold-start or bundle cost is saved. There is also a new risk: if an app module fails to load and nothing awaits that key, its rejected promise is an unhandled rejection. Before, the same failure surfaced at import time. Store thunks instead (`applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and have callers write `await appStore[key]?.()`.

findings.title: The `forEach(async …)` callback moves `getCalendar` errors outside the `try/catch`.
findings.body: Before this change, a synchronous throw from `getCalendar` (for example a CalendarService constructor failing on a bad credential) was caught and logged by the surrounding `try/catch`. Now the callback is async and `forEach` ignores the promises it returns. Such errors become unhandled promise rejections that are not logged here and can crash a Node process running with the default unhandled-rejection mode. The deletions are also never awaited. Fix: `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` inside the `try`.

findings.title: The `forEach(async …)` callback moves `getCalendar` errors outside the `try/catch`.
findings.body: Same problem as in vital's `reschedule.ts`. The async callback's promises are dropped by `forEach`, so a `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` failure is no longer caught by the surrounding `try/catch`. It becomes an unhandled rejection instead. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the `try`.

findings.title: `getCalendarCredentials` now puts a Promise in `calendar`, which breaks callers that use it directly.
findings.body: `getCalendar` is now async, but this function still stores its result in `calendar` without awaiting it. `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to await it. Any other caller of `getCalendarCredentials` that reads `item.calendar` is not updated, and I couldn't see whether such callers exist. In those callers, `if (calendar)` is always true for a Promise, and `calendar.listCalendars()` or `getAvailability()` throws `is not a function`. A rejected `getCalendar` promise that no caller awaits also becomes an unhandled rejection. Fix: make `getCalendarCredentials` async and resolve the calendars with `Promise.all`, or audit every caller.

findings.title: The `forEach(async …)` callback drops the promises, so `getCalendar` failures become unhandled rejections.
findings.body: `getCalendar` now runs inside an async callback whose promise `forEach` discards. Any error from `getCalendar` or from the deletions no longer reaches the request's error handling and becomes an unhandled rejection. The handler also no longer waits for the async credential resolution before it returns. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))`.
